images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a polished high-fidelity desktop application design image for Board, Transit's inspection interface. This is a visual design study with synthetic data, not a screenshot of an implemented product. Produce one landscape 16:10 image, ideally 1920 x 1200, showing the actual flat application screen edge to edge, not a laptop or a perspective view of a monitor.
Visual direction: an exquisitely drawn topographic atlas meets a precise developer inspection tool. Warm paper #f3f2eb, deep blue-green ink #192f34, muted sage #586965, hairline boundaries #d5d9ce, restrained amber #dba854 for attention and selection. Sophisticated Swiss sans-serif typography, monospaced identifiers and tabular numerals, crisp legible text. Restrained elevation and shadows, airy but information-dense. No neon, glassmorphism, generic KPI dashboard, oversized marketing headlines, decorative charts, or photorealistic mountains.
Shared application shell: narrow 64px icon navigation rail on left with small B monogram; 64px header with "Board", scope "demo · Realm 1", a centered search field "Find a process or resource", mode toggle "Browse | Map". Header and controls are always flat HTML-like surfaces. A slim footer includes "Design study · Synthetic data" and the observation "Position 240 · Policy 7". All controls are for inspection: open, inspect, focus, copy link, refresh. No create, edit, delete, restart, retry work, pause process, publish, login or avatar.
Shared data: one realm, eight processes on one displayed page, 84 pending inputs total on that page. Process 04 (PID 4) is the selected object with 36 pending, lifecycle "Running", generation 3 and state revision 18. Process pending counts: 01=18, 02=12, 03=8, 04=36, 05=6, 06=4, 07=0, 08=0. Display aliases are synthetic, not registered names. Running is a lifecycle, never label it "worker healthy". All tallies are explicitly for the displayed page, not realm totals.
For map scenes, maintain the same recognizable arrangement across zoom levels: selected Process 04 in center; Process 01 upper left; 02 upper middle; 03 upper right; 05 right; 06 lower right; 07 lower left; 08 left. Use a single large subtly hexagonal realm perimeter. No other realms. Process markers are small circles, state resources are small rectangular plates. Selected Process 04 has an associated "Resource 12", revision 9, lower-left of its marker. Relationship lines mean explicit recorded evidence only, not proximity. No fabricated network traffic animation, capacity, latency, ETA, CPU or RAM measures. No heat colors suggesting that a large backlog proves failure.
Text is short, accurate and clearly typeset; prefer fewer legible labels to tiny fabricated text. UI elements should feel implementable and deliberate.
Screen: relief overview, Map selected. The main canvas occupies roughly 70% of the width and a 300px right inspector occupies the remainder. Title above canvas "Realm overview". A layer dropdown reads "Elevation: pending inputs". A compact caption reads "8 displayed · 84 pending · Page only".
Render a beautiful restrained shallow oblique relief map INSIDE the flat UI: one hexagonal paper landform, three principal teal-gray embossed mounds with fine contour lines; tallest peak anchored to selected Process 04 at the center, lower mounds at Processes 01 and 02 upper left. The terrain should genuinely appear raised, like a precisely lit physical relief atlas, while remaining schematic rather than geographic. Eight circular process marks at the specified stable positions; only three or four major names need prominent labels. Small source-anchored callouts: "04 / 36 pending", "01 / 18", "02 / 12". Realm boundary label "demo / Realm 1". No all-to-all edges.
Right inspector heading "Process 04", subheading "PID 4". Small Running lifecycle badge. Large but restrained "36" with label "Pending inputs". Rows "Generation 3", "State revision 18". Association link "Resource 12 · revision 9". Outline action "Open process". Beneath, a miniature flat locator showing the selected central location.
Bottom-left map legend: "Pending inputs per process" with levels 0, 12, 24, 36 and small neutral elevation swatches. Bottom-right plus, minus and fit controls. A small view badge "Overview · relief". Leave enough open paper around the landform to read its silhouette. This is the hero image of the design proposal.
